text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today to $127.30, extending a week-long decline that has now reached 7.3%. The main driver appears to be oil price weakness: U.S. crude dropped nearly 8% last week after the U.S. and Iran held talks at the United Nations, with Iran proposing conditions for a ceasefire. Even though those talks broke down—Trump rejected Iran's offer and signaled renewed military action—the initial hope for de-escalation had already pressured prices lower, and oil has stayed soft at $96.41 per barrel today, well below the $114.89 price for global crude.

The broader backdrop is volatile geopolitical risk with conflicting signals. Saudi Arabia is ramping up exports despite ongoing attacks on its infrastructure from Iran-backed groups, which usually tightens supply and supports prices. However, the market seems to be giving more weight right now to the possibility of diplomatic resolution, even a fragile one, over the supply-disruption story. That's kept crude under pressure and dragged down the stock along with it.
